The source is compiled by nvcc (CUDA\n# kernels), so host-compiler flags are forwarded with -Xcompiler.\ntarget_compile_options(spmv PRIVATE\n    $<$<COMPILE_LANGUAGE:CXX>:-O3 -march=native -Wall -Wextra>\n    $<$<COMPILE_LANGUAGE:CUDA>:-O3>\n    $<$<COMPILE_LANGUAGE:CUDA>:-Xcompiler=-march=native>\n    $<$<COMPILE_LANGUAGE:CUDA>:-Xcompiler=-Wall>\n    $<$<COMPILE_LANGUAGE:CUDA>:-Xcompiler=-Wextra>\n    $<$<COMPILE_LANGUAGE:CUDA>:-Xcompiler=-fopenmp>\n)\n\ntarget_link_libraries(spmv PRIVATE\n    MPI::MPI_CXX\n    OpenMP::OpenMP_CXX\n    CUDA::cudart\n    m\n)\n"},"output":"Wrote file successfully.","metadata":{"diagnostics":{},"filepath":"/home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/spmv_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_hybrid_r5/spmv/CMakeLists.txt","exists":true,"truncated":false},"title":"home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/spmv_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_hybrid_r5/spmv/CMakeLists.txt","time":{"start":1793153742903,"end":1793153742939}},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"caller":{"type":"direct"}}},"id":"prt_1804ab21d001R44mDGjHkrlU7n","sessionID":"ses_e7fb79fd6ffe0JOcgZJvYEPM06","messageID":"msg_18049d650001PrlSKhoUGoZUCv"}}

{"type":"tool_use","timestamp":1793153775904,"sessionID":"ses_e7fb79fd6ffe0JOcgZJvYEPM06","part":{"type":"tool","tool":"write","callID":"toolu_01G3PRfhgJ9JA6f8HAKZQBKV","state":{"status":"completed","input":{"filePath":"/home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/spmv_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_hybrid_r5/spmv/spmv.cpp","content":"// Hybrid MPI + OpenMP + CUDA sparse matrix-vector multiplication benchmark.\n//\n// Decomposition:\n//   * MPI:    rows are block-partitioned across ranks. The dense vector is\n//             replicated (broadcast once); each rank owns a contiguous block\n//             of matrix rows and the matching block of the output. No\n//             communication happens inside the timed iterations.\n//   * CUDA:   each rank drives one GPU (localRank % deviceCount). The leading\n//             rows of the local block are computed on the GPU using a sliced\n//             ELLPACK layout (slices of 32 rows, column-major within a slice)\n//             so that warp accesses to values and column indices are coalesced.\n//   * OpenMP: the trailing rows of the local block are computed on host\n//             threads concurrently with the GPU kernel.\n//\n// Every output row is accumulated in the same left-to-right order as the\n// original serial code, using an explicit fused multiply-add on both the host\n// and the device, so results are bit-identical regardless of which resource\n// computed a row.\n\n#include <mpi.h>\n#include <omp.h>\n#include <cuda_runtime.h>\n\n#include <algorithm>\n#include <chrono>\n#include <cmath>\n#include <cstdint>\n#include <cstdio>\n#include <cstdlib>\n#include <cstring>\n#include <vector>\n\n#include \"../common/results_output.hpp\"\n\nusing index_t = uint32_t;\n\n// Constants\nconstexpr double MAX_RELATIVE_ERROR = 0.02;\n\n// Every CPU_ROW_DIVISOR-th row of a rank's block (1/16 of its rows) is\n// computed by OpenMP host threads; the remainder is computed on the GPU.\nconstexpr index_t CPU_ROW_DIVISOR = 16;\n\n// Rows per sliced-ELL slice; equal to the warp size so slices map to warps.\nconstexpr index_t SLICE_HEIGHT = 32;\n\n// Threads per CUDA block (a multiple of SLICE_HEIGHT).\nconstexpr unsigned int CUDA_BLOCK_SIZE = 128;\n\n// ****************************************************************************\n// Error handling helpers\n// ****************************************************************************\n#define MPI_CHECK(call)                                                        \\\n    do {                                                                       \\\n        const int err_ = (call);                                               \\\n        if (err_ != MPI_SUCCESS) {                                             \\\n            fprintf(stderr, \"MPI error at %s:%d\\n\", __FILE__, __LINE__);       \\\n            MPI_Abort(MPI_COMM_WORLD, 1);                                      \\\n        }                                                                      \\\n    } while (0)\n\n#define CUDA_CHECK(call)                                                       \\\n    do {                                                                       \\\n        const cudaError_t err_ = (call);                                       \\\n        if (err_ != cudaSuccess) {                                             \\\n            fprintf(stderr, \"CUDA error at %s:%d: %s\\n\", __FILE__, __LINE__,   \\\n                    cudaGetErrorString(err_));                                 \\\n            MPI_Abort(MPI_COMM_WORLD, 1);                                      \\\n        }                                                                      \\\n    } while (0)\n\n// ****************************************************************************\n// Function: fill\n//\n// Purpose:\n//   Initialize array with random values\n//\n// Arguments:\n//   A: pointer to the array to initialize\n//   n: number of elements in the array\n//   maxVal: specifies range of random values [0, maxVal]\n//\n// ****************************************************************************\nvoid fill(double* A, const index_t n, const double maxVal) {\n    for (index_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        A[i] = maxVal * (rand() / (static_cast<double>(RAND_MAX) + 1.0));\n    }\n}\n\n// ****************************************************************************\n// Function: initRandomMatrix\n//\n// Purpose:\n//   Assigns random positions to a given number of elements in a square\n//   matrix. The function encodes these positions in compressed sparse\n//   row (CSR) format.\n//\n// Arguments:\n//   cols:          array for column indexes of elements (size should be = n)\n//   rowDelimiters: array of size dim+1 holding indices to rows;\n//                  last element is the index one past the last element\n//   n:             number of nonzero elements\n//   dim:           number of rows/columns in the matrix\n//\n// ****************************************************************************\nvoid initRandomMatrix(index_t* cols, index_t* rowDelimiters, const index_t n, const index_t dim) {\n    index_t nnzAssigned = 0;\n\n    // Figure out the probability that a nonzero should be assigned\n    double prob = static_cast<double>(n) / (static_cast<double>(dim) * static_cast<double>(dim));\n\n    // Seed random number generator\n    srand(8675309);\n\n    // Randomly decide whether entry i,j gets a value, but ensure n values are assigned\n    bool fillRemaining = false;\n    for (index_t i = 0; i < dim; ++i) {\n        rowDelimiters[i] = nnzAssigned;\n        for (index_t j = 0; j < dim; ++j) {\n            index_t numEntriesLeft = (dim * dim) - ((i * dim) + j);\n            index_t needToAssign = n - nnzAssigned;\n            if (numEntriesLeft <= needToAssign) {\n                fillRemaining = true;\n            }\n            double randVal = static_cast<double>(rand()) / RAND_MAX;\n            if ((nnzAssigned < n && randVal <= prob) || fillRemaining) {\n                // Assign (i,j) a value\n                cols[nnzAssigned] = j;\n                nnzAssigned++;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    // Convention: put the number of non-zeroes at the end of the row delimiters array\n    rowDelimiters[dim] = n;\n}\n\n// ****************************************************************************\n// Function: spmvCpu\n//\n// Purpose:\n//   Serial reference implementation of sparse matrix-vector multiplication\n//   using CSR format. Used only for validation.\n//\n// Arguments:\n//   val: array holding the non-zero values for the matrix\n//   cols: array of column indices for each element\n//   rowDelimiters: array of size dim+1 holding indices to rows;\n//                  last element is the index one past the last element\n//   vec: dense vector of size dim to be used for multiplication\n//   dim: number of rows/columns in the matrix\n//   out: output - result from the spmv calculation\n//\n// ****************************************************************************\nvoid spmvCpu(const double* val, const index_t* cols, const index_t* rowDelimiters,\n             const double* vec, const index_t dim, double* out) {\n    for (index_t i = 0; i < dim; ++i) {\n        double t = 0.0;\n        for (index_t j = rowDelimiters[i]; j < rowDelimiters[i + 1]; ++j) {\n            const auto col = cols[j];\n            t += val[j] * vec[col];\n        }\n        out[i] = t;\n    }\n}\n\n// ****************************************************************************\n// Function: spmvCpuOmp\n//\n// Purpose:\n//   OpenMP-parallel CSR SpMV over the row range [rowBegin, rowEnd). Each row is\n//   accumulated sequentially, so the result matches the device kernel exactly.\n//\n// Arguments:\n//   val, cols, rowDelimiters: local CSR arrays (rowDelimiters indexes val/cols)\n//   vec: dense input vector\n//   rowBegin, rowEnd: half-open row range to compute\n//   out: output vector (indexed by row)\n//\n// ****************************************************************************\nvoid spmvCpuOmp(const double* val, const index_t* cols, const index_t* rowDelimiters,\n                const double* vec, const index_t rowBegin, const index_t rowEnd, double* out) {\n#pragma omp parallel for schedule(static)\n    for (index_t i = rowBegin; i < rowEnd; ++i) {\n        double t = 0.0;\n        for (index_t j = rowDelimiters[i]; j < rowDelimiters[i + 1]; ++j) {\n            t = std::fma(val[j], vec[cols[j]], t);\n        }\n        out[i] = t;\n    }\n}\n\n// ****************************************************************************\n// Sliced ELLPACK representation for the GPU\n// ****************************************************************************\nstruct EllSlices {\n    std::vector<double> val;        // slice-major, then column-major within slice\n    std::vector<index_t> cols;      // same layout as val\n    std::vector<uint64_t> sliceOff; // offset of each slice in val/cols (size numSlices+1)\n    std::vector<index_t> rowLen;    // number of nonzeros in each row\n};\n\n// ****************************************************************************\n// Function: buildEll\n//\n// Purpose:\n//   Converts the first numRows rows of a CSR matrix into sliced ELLPACK.\n//   Entry k of row r in slice s is stored at sliceOff[s] + k*SLICE_HEIGHT +\n//   (r % SLICE_HEIGHT), so consecutive lanes of a warp access consecutive\n//   memory. Padding slots are zero and are never read (rowLen bounds the loop).\n//\n// ****************************************************************************\nEllSlices buildEll(const double* csrVal, const index_t* csrCols, const index_t* rowDelimiters,\n                   const index_t numRows) {\n    EllSlices e;\n    const index_t numSlices = (numRows + SLICE_HEIGHT - 1) / SLICE_HEIGHT;\n\n    e.rowLen.resize(numRows);\n    for (index_t r = 0; r < numRows; ++r) {\n        e.rowLen[r] = rowDelimiters[r + 1] - rowDelimiters[r];\n    }\n\n    e.sliceOff.assign(numSlices + 1, 0);\n    for (index_t s = 0; s < numSlices; ++s) {\n        const index_t first = s * SLICE_HEIGHT;\n        const index_t last = std::min<index_t>(first + SLICE_HEIGHT, numRows);\n        index_t width = 0;\n        for (index_t r = first; r < last; ++r) {\n            width = std::max(width, e.rowLen[r]);\n        }\n        e.sliceOff[s + 1] = e.sliceOff[s] + static_cast<uint64_t>(SLICE_HEIGHT) * width;\n    }\n\n    const uint64_t total = e.sliceOff[numSlices];\n    e.val.assign(total, 0.0);\n    e.cols.assign(total, 0);\n\n#pragma omp parallel for schedule(dynamic, 4)\n    for (index_t s = 0; s < numSlices; ++s) {\n        const index_t first = s * SLICE_HEIGHT;\n        const index_t last = std::min<index_t>(first + SLICE_HEIGHT, numRows);\n        for (index_t r = first; r < last; ++r) {\n            const index_t lane = r - first;\n            const index_t begin = rowDelimiters[r];\n            for (index_t k = 0; k < e.rowLen[r]; ++k) {\n                const uint64_t dst = e.sliceOff[s] + static_cast<uint64_t>(k) * SLICE_HEIGHT + lane;\n                e.val[dst] = csrVal[begin + k];\n                e.cols[dst] = csrCols[begin + k];\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    return e;\n}\n\n// ****************************************************************************\n// CUDA kernel: one thread per row over sliced ELLPACK data.\n// Accumulation order per row matches the host kernel (fma chain, k ascending).\n// ****************************************************************************\n__global__ void spmvEllKernel(const double* __restrict__ val, const index_t* __restrict__ cols,\n                              const uint64_t* __restrict__ sliceOff,\n                              const index_t* __restrict__ rowLen,\n                              const double* __restrict__ x, const index_t numRows,\n                              double* __restrict__ y) {\n    const index_t row = blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;\n    if (row >= numRows) {\n        return;\n    }\n    const index_t lane = row % SLICE_HEIGHT;\n    const uint64_t base = sliceOff[row / SLICE_HEIGHT] + lane;\n    const index_t len = rowLen[row];\n\n    double t = 0.0;\n    for (index_t k = 0; k < len; ++k) {\n        const uint64_t idx = base + static_cast<uint64_t>(k) * SLICE_HEIGHT;\n        t = __fma_rn(val[idx], __ldg(&x[cols[idx]]), t);\n    }\n    y[row] = t;\n}\n\n// ****************************************************************************\n// Class: GpuEllSpmv\n//\n// Purpose:\n//   Owns the device copy of a rank's GPU row block (matrix in sliced ELL, and\n//   the replicated input vector) and the stream used for kernel launches.\n//\n// ****************************************************************************\nclass GpuEllSpmv {\n  public:\n    GpuEllSpmv(const EllSlices& ell, const std::vector<double>& x, const index_t rows)\n        : rows_(rows) {\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaStreamCreate(&stream_));\n        if (rows_ == 0) {\n            return;\n        }\n        const size_t numSlices = ell.sliceOff.size() - 1;\n        d_val_ = allocAndCopy(ell.val.data(), ell.val.size());\n        d_cols_ = allocAndCopy(ell.cols.data(), allocAndCopy(x.data(), x.size());\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc(&d_y_, std::max<size_t>(rows_, 1) * sizeof(double)));\n        (void)numSlices;\n    }\n\n    ~GpuEllSpmv() {\n {"type":"reasoning","timestamp":1793155431358,"sessionID":"ses_e7fb79fd6ffe0JOcgZJvYEPM06","part":{"id":"prt_1806459520012epyHgK5RBOiCj","messageID":"msg_18064552c001jDXXnU83GNOPnb","sessionID":"ses_e7fb79fd6ffe0JOcgZJvYEPM06","type":"reasoning","text":"I'm noticing a huge timing discrepancy: div=8 runs at 0.35ms/iter while div=4 takes 11ms/iter despite similar thread counts, which doesn't match my expectations given the nnz and thread calculations. Something about the div=4 configuration must be causing inefficiency that I need to dig into further.\n\nWorking through the bandwidth numbers for div=8, the CPU side computes out to roughly 115GB/s which seems plausible if data fits mostly in L3, and the GPU side lands near 800GB/s which is close to the 3090's theoretical peak of 936GB/s — meaning div=8 is essentially bandwidth-bound and performing excellently, while something is clearly off with the smaller div configurations.\n\nWith the heavy CPU share case at 11ms, I'm suspecting the real culprit is OpenMP thread wake-up overhead — with ~200+ threads spawned per parallel region, futex-based wakeup latency could easily add a couple milliseconds if threads have gone idle between iterations, which would explain why smaller CPU shares (fewer threads) run comparatively faster despite doing proportionally less work.\n\nSo the fix isn't necessarily algorithmic but about tuning NNZ_PER_CPU_THREAD so fewer, larger-granularity threads get spawned — I'm thinking something like 256K nnz per thread instead of 32K, capping team size around 16-32 threads. I'll hold off finalizing defaults until I see the rest of the sweep across div=8, 16, and 32 to confirm which config keeps CPU work cheap enough to stay GPU-bound.\n\n","time":{"start":1793155422546,"end":1793155431320},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}

I'll stick with div=16 since it balances well across different rank counts - 7ms for np=1 and 4ms for np=4, even though the GPU is underutilized in the latter case. The poor div=4 performance likely comes from thread-team overhead.\n\nThere's a real robustness concern though: on machines with default MPI binding (bind-to core), threads get limited to whatever omp_get_num_procs() returns under the affinity mask, often just 2. With only 2 CPU threads, the CPU-side work becomes the bottleneck rather than the GPU, which could make this slower than a GPU-only approach entirely. Since the thread count is constrained by the binding mask and can't be fixed in code, the practical mitigation is documenting that users should pass `--bind-to none` or similar binding flags. I'll leave the divisor as-is rather than trying to make the CPU/GPU split adaptive to thread count, and just document the binding requirement clearly.\n\nNow I want to run the correctness check script alongside timing tests under default binding conditions, rebuild the main build directory, and kick off a background sanity run across several configs since the comparison script takes a few minutes.\n\n","time":{"start":1793155532509,"end":1793155540175},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}

{"type":"reasoning","timestamp":1793155870647,"sessionID":"ses_e7fb79fd6ffe0JOcgZJvYEPM06","part":{"id":"prt_1806b18a3001Qtg7b0D0fk0w7m","messageID":"msg_1806b1496001m3O6IXUCm6J1hh","sessionID":"ses_e7fb79fd6ffe0JOcgZJvYEPM06","type":"reasoning","text":"I'm pulling together a summary of the changes to spmv's CMakeLists.txt and spmv.cpp, noting the design approach, verification via bit-identical hashes across process counts and sizes, and the performance gains—from an 832ms baseline down to 7ms at np=1 and 4ms at np=4, roughly a 119x speedup—along with some caveats around launch behavior.\n\nI need to mention requiring `--bind-to none` to avoid Open MPI's default binding collapsing the OpenMP team down to just two threads, which otherwise would slow things to 44ms, plus the fixed CPU split ratio tuned specifically for this machine. I should also flag the pre-existing overflow crash at n>=65536 that was left untouched, the raised CMake minimum version, and how the thread-per-row GPU kernel and serial rank-0 matrix generation limit parallelism for smaller per-GPU row counts, while the deliberate choice to preserve exact summation order trades off some GPU parallelism compared to a warp-per-row approach. Finally, I want to note that I built everything in scratch space rather than the workspace, and that output.txt is just the harness log, untouched by my changes.\n\n","time":{"start":1793155864739,"end":1793155870603},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}
